## Overview

Predicts the next visible passes of the International Space Station over your
house, shows them on a dashboard widget, and can trigger a scene right before
one starts — perfect for "go look outside" automations.

### What it shows

The **ISS Passes** widget displays:

- a photo of the station, and how long until the next visible pass, with its
  maximum elevation;
- the next few passes, with their time, duration and the direction the ISS
  rises from (local time, in the language of your Gladys);
- whether the ISS is visible tonight, and whether the orbital data used to
  compute passes is fresh.

A pass is only shown as visible when the ISS is above the horizon, your house
is in the dark, and the ISS itself is still lit by the sun — the same
conditions that make it a bright, fast-moving "star" in the evening or
early-morning sky.

### Automations

- **Trigger: "ISS pass starting"** — fires shortly before a visible pass
  begins. Optionally filter by the direction it rises from. Use it to turn on
  a "look up!" notification, or to switch off outdoor lights that would spoil
  the view.
- **Action: "Get next ISS pass"** — fetches the next predicted pass on demand,
  for scenes that want to announce it (e.g. a voice message) rather than react
  to it.

Both expose the pass as variables. For a message, prefer the ready-to-read
ones, written in the **Scene language** of the configuration and in your
local time: `start_date` (e.g. "Monday, September 28"), `start_hour`
(e.g. "07:49 PM") and `direction_name` (e.g. "west"). `direction` (compass
code, e.g. "W") stays available for scenes that compare it. For example "The ISS passes on _start_date_ at _start_hour_,
rising in the _direction_name_." gives "The ISS passes on Monday, September 28
at 07:49 PM, rising in the west.", for a notification as well as a voice
message.

## Prerequisites

- **Gladys 5.2 or later.** The house picker of the configuration needs Gladys
  5.2 (the dashboard widget and the scene trigger/action ship with Gladys 5.1);
  on an earlier version the integration cannot be installed.
- A **house with a location** in Gladys (house settings, map): the passes are
  computed for its coordinates.
- **Internet access** from the Gladys server, to download the orbital data
  from Celestrak.

### No API key needed

Orbital data (TLE) is fetched from [Celestrak](https://celestrak.org/), a free
public source — nothing to sign up for.

## Configuration

| Key               | Default   | Description                                                                |
| ----------------- | --------- | -------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| House             | (empty)   | House the passes are predicted for (see below).                            |
| Minimum elevation | 10°       | Passes that never rise above this angle are ignored.                       |
| Prediction window | 5 days    | How far ahead passes are predicted (3, 5 or 7 days).                       |
| Scene lead time   | 5 minutes | How long before a pass starts the "ISS pass starting" trigger fires (≤60). |
| Scene language    | French    | Language of the date, time and direction handed to scenes.                 |

The integration needs your house's location, granted automatically when you
install it (no address to type in).

With several houses in Gladys, pick the one to watch the sky from in
**House**. Left empty, or if the chosen house is deleted or has no location
anymore, the first house (in alphabetical order) that has a location is used.
Make sure the house is located in Gladys (house settings, map): a house
without a location cannot be used.

## Troubleshooting

- **Status "Initialization failed, check the integration logs."**: the
  integration could not read the location of your house or download the
  orbital data. It tries again on its own, waiting a bit longer each time (up
  to 30 minutes). Open the **Logs** tab of the integration to see why:
  - `No house with a known location`: no house in Gladys has a location.
    Place your house on the map in its settings.
  - `Celestrak request failed with status …`, or a timeout: Celestrak could
    not be reached. Check the internet access of the Gladys server.
- **The widget only shows "Visible soon: No"**: no visible pass was found in
  the prediction window. The ISS is only visible under the conditions
  described above, so several days in a row without a visible pass are
  normal. You can lower the **Minimum elevation** or widen the **Prediction
  window** to 7 days. The widget also looks like this while the integration
  has no house location or no orbital data yet (see the previous point).
- **"Orbital data: Stale" on the widget**: the orbital data is more than
  24 hours old, because Celestrak could not be reached. The integration keeps
  computing the passes with the last data it got and tries again every
  6 hours. Check the internet access of the Gladys server if it lasts.
- **The passes are computed for the wrong house**: the house chosen in
  **House** no longer exists or has no location anymore. The logs then show
  `The chosen house "…" is unknown or has no location, using "…" instead`.
  Pick a located house in **House**, or place the chosen one on the map.
- **The house moved, but the passes did not change**: the location is read
  when the integration starts and each time you save its configuration. Save
  the configuration again.
- **The "ISS pass starting" trigger did not fire**: it only fires for
  visible passes that rise above the **Minimum elevation** and, when its
  filter has directions selected, only for those directions. A pass whose trigger time (start minus the **Scene
  lead time**) is already over when the integration starts or when you save
  the configuration is skipped.
- **"Get next ISS pass" gives empty variables**: no visible pass is predicted
  in the prediction window. The **A pass was found** variable is then false:
  check it in your scene before using the others.

## Parámetros de configuración

Estos son los parámetros que ISS Overhead te pide en su pantalla de configuración en Gladys.

| Parámetro | Tipo | Obligatorio | Descripción |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| House | `select` | No | House the passes are predicted for. Left empty, the first house with a location is used. |
| Minimum elevation (°) | `number` | No | Passes rising below this elevation angle are ignored. |
| Prediction window | `select` | No | How many days ahead to predict passes for. |
| Scene lead time (minutes) | `number` | No | How long before a pass starts the "ISS pass starting" trigger fires. |
| Scene language | `select` | No | Language of the date, time and direction handed to your scenes (notifications, voice messages). |

## Cómo instalar ISS Overhead en Gladys

1. En Gladys, abre **Integraciones**: ISS Overhead aparece en el catálogo junto a las integraciones nativas, con una insignia de comunidad.
2. Haz clic en **Instalar**. Gladys descarga la imagen Docker (`ghcr.io/cicoub13/gladys-iss:0.5.1`), la ejecuta en un entorno aislado del núcleo y genera la interfaz de la integración (dispositivos, descubrimiento y configuración).
3. Abre la pantalla de **Configuración** de la integración, rellena los parámetros y guarda.
4. También puedes instalarla directamente desde la URL de su repositorio: [https://github.com/cicoub13/gladys-iss](https://github.com/cicoub13/gladys-iss).

ISS Overhead requiere Gladys `>=5.2.0`. El catálogo de Gladys se actualiza cada hora, así que una nueva versión está disponible como máximo una hora después de publicarse.

¿Todavía no usas Gladys? Es gratuito y de código abierto: [sigue la guía de instalación](/es/docs/) para empezar.

## Sobre las integraciones externas

ISS Overhead es una **integración externa**: una integración comunitaria empaquetada como contenedor Docker y publicada en GitHub. Gladys la instala con un clic y la ejecuta en un entorno aislado del núcleo. La publica y mantiene [cicoub13](https://github.com/cicoub13), no el equipo principal de Gladys.
